key_insight: The best surrogate depends on the fracture task: FNO and Latent DeepONet lead on Dataset 1, while diffusion leads on Dataset 2 at a steep inference cost.
engineering_relevance: Fracture-Bench supports task-specific surrogate selection for uncertainty quantification, inverse analysis and design by comparing accuracy, speed and model size.
method: Benchmark 1,000 AT2 simulations of a notched-hole plate and 4,000 PF-CZM simulations of a pre-cracked plate with stiffness-contrasting inclusions.
Train FNO, DeepONet, Latent DeepONet, UNet and conditional diffusion models on identical splits.
Evaluate a common metric within each dataset alongside training time, inference time and model size.
evidence_signal: FNO and Latent DeepONet achieve mean test errors of order 10⁻⁶ on Dataset 1; on Dataset 2, diffusion has about one-sixth of UNet's error but takes 706 s per prediction versus 6 ms.
watch_item: Average errors can obscure near-bifurcation failures: initial cracks less than one grid cell apart can produce qualitatively different paths, and errors concentrate after crack localization.
paper_title: Fracture-Bench: A Controlled Benchmark Suite for Machine Learning Surrogates in Phase-Field Fracture Mechanics
